questions.question: Which abilities are harmed by drinking alcohol?

options.text: Judgment
Ability to reason
Vision
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms all skills needed to drive safely. These include judgment, reaction time, vision, reasoning, and concentration. Alcohol is absorbed through the stomach lining, enters the bloodstream, and reaches your brain within minutes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay away from them. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures that might make them more angry. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can safely do to stay out of danger.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or their vehicles properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful.
Have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or their vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It harms judgment, vision, concentration, awareness of reality, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a steady green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You may continue, but drive at a speed that lets you slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Don't stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train in sight or sound, you must stop if:

options.text: A stop sign is posted.
The crossing gate is down.
The crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagperson signals you to stop, or a train is visible or dangerously close. Never race a train.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. To avoid getting drowsy, don't stare at any one spot for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms many skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time and clear vision. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, lowers caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss your exit. Do not stop or back up on the highway. Do not swerve across lanes at the last second or cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving ability.
No, it helps keep the driver alert.
Yes, it is a distracting activity.
No, it is not a distracting activity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distracting activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?

options.text: It slows your reflexes and reaction time.
It puts you to sleep.
It wakes you up.
It improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Which of these can impair your driving ability?

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Lack of sleep.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, and drowsiness can all impair your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: You feel angry after work. What should you do before driving home?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the interstate to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar and have a few drinks before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to relax before driving. Driving while emotional or upset is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: If you hit a parked car with no one inside, what should you do?

options.text: You can drive away without stopping.
Find the owner or leave a written note with your information.
You do not need to contact your insurance company.
You can leave without leaving any notice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find the owner or leave a written note with your information.
questions.explanation: You must stop immediately after hitting an unattended vehicle. Find the owner or leave a written note. Include your full name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn allowed.
No U-turn allowed.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that left turns are not permitted.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
All passengers must use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in a rear seat with proper restraints. Never place a rear-facing infant car seat in the front of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: What is important to know about trucks?

options.text: They need longer distances to stop than cars.
They pass faster than cars going downhill.
They turn in a smaller radius than cars.
They pass faster than cars going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need longer distances to stop than cars.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are larger and heavier, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Any distraction that takes your attention, eyes, or hands away from driving can cause a crash.

questions.question: When passing a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Move back to your lane and slow down right away.
Give the truck plenty of space before moving back to your lane.
Move back to your lane whenever you want.
Move back to your lane when you are right next to the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the truck plenty of space before moving back to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not cut back into the truck's lane too quickly. Wait until you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror. Do not slow down. Trucks need almost twice as much space to stop as regular vehicles.

questions.question: You must always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals tell other drivers what you are doing and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, slow down and safely pull to the side of the road. Stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can get out of its way.

questions.question: Motorcycles on the road:

options.text: Have the same rights and responsibilities as larger vehicles.
Do not need to follow the rules of the road.
Must always yield to larger vehicles.
Are not a safety concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars and trucks. Drivers must respect the rights of motorcycles on the road.

questions.question: When should you check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower decision-making.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol weakens your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if someone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad track?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly go under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing the tracks. Watch for warning signals and only cross when you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a T intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to traffic crossing your path.
Have the right-of-way.
Push your way into traffic.
Back up and turn around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic crossing your path.
questions.explanation: At a T intersection, stop and yield the right-of-way to vehicles on the crossroad. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:

options.text: Leaving extra time for your trip.
Following posted speed limits.
Using proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, follow speed limits, and leave plenty of time for your trip.
